key_facts.claim: Ninja Van Singapore announced a restructuring that cut about 12% of its local workforce in August 2025.

evidence.quote: Ninja Van lays off 12% of local workforce in latest restructuring exercise
Ninja Van cuts 12% of Singapore workforce after 2 rounds of layoffs in 2024

key_facts.claim: The company said the layoffs were part of a long‑term plan to strengthen its business model and ensure sustainable growth.

evidence.quote: part of a long‑term plan to strengthen its business model and ensure sustainable growth
the job cuts are part of the company’s long‑term effort to strengthen its business model

key_facts.claim: Affected employees will receive severance packages, extended medical insurance and mental‑health support until 31 December.

evidence.quote: Employees ... will receive severance packages, extended health insurance and mental health support until 31 December
Medical insurance and mental health support will also be extended till the end of the year

key_facts.claim: Ninja Van operates in multiple Southeast Asian markets and delivers millions of parcels daily.

evidence.quote: Founded in 2014, Ninja Van currently operates in six markets across Southeast Asia and delivers 2 million parcels a day

key_facts.claim: The company raised US$578 million in a Series E round in 2021, giving it a unicorn valuation.

evidence.quote: It has raised US$578 million in a Series E round in 2021 ... lifting the company’s valuation to “well over” US$1 billion

positive_signals.claim: Ninja Van is a well‑funded logistics unicorn with a large parcel‑delivery operation.

evidence.quote: It has raised US$578 million in a Series E round in 2021 ... turned it into a unicorn
delivers 2 million parcels a day, according to its website

positive_signals.claim: The company continues to post job openings for Singapore‑based roles, indicating ongoing operations.

evidence.quote: A check on Ninja Van’s job openings on its website showed it still has positions open for more than 10 Singapore‑based roles

red_flags.claim: Multiple customer reviews describe poor service, unresponsive support channels, and delivery failures.

evidence.quote: All help lines ... seem bogus. A live agent is never with you to answer your complaints
I tried to escalate this via Ninja Van Singapore's live chat, the customer service was utterly useless and dismissive

red_flags.claim: Recent large‑scale layoffs suggest financial or operational stress.

evidence.quote: Ninja Van has laid off about 12% of its Singapore workforce yesterday (August 12) in its latest round of job cuts
reports emerged that Ninja Van is currently in talks to raise US$80 million ... could cut its valuation by about half

Customer‑review sites provide consistent negative feedback about service. No official registry entry was found for the exact name, but the weight of consistent media coverage supports the company's existence and activities.
